land.text: the land west of the Ural where 'Russia let Sultan Bukey, son of Nur Ali, settle permanently' in 1801 with some 7,500 families of the Junior Zhuz

predecessors.note: The Junior Zhuz is the small-horde dossier; the grant of land was Russian.

land.text: the area 'gradually came under Russian civil administration' after the khan's office was abolished in 1845

capitals.name: Khan Ordasy (Khan Headquarters)
capitals.note: BH infobox: capital Khan Ordasy; Jangir founded Khan-Kala (Khanskaya Stavka) in 1827 and the summer headquarters Tor-gun-Kala in 1841. The page gives no coordinates; those are the gazetteer's Zhanibek, the researcher's stand-in.

rulers.name: Jangir
rulers.title: Khan
rulers.note: Recognised 'by letter of Alexander I in 1823', installed in 1824; the last khan.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row: BH gives 'about 71,000 square kilometers' and 'on the western side of the Ural'; the radius of 150 km round Zhanibek (about 71,000 km2) matches the area but its centre is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: 1801: Sultan Bukey settles with 7,500 families west of the Ural. 'In 1801, Russia let Sultan Bukey ... settle permanently on the western side of the Ural' with some 7,500 families of the Junior Zhuz; the khanate 'officially existed from 1801 to 1845'. The place is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Bukey Horde's lands on the western side of the Ural, about 71,000 km2 (BH); the centre is the researcher's

ledger.note: 1845: the Bukey khanate ends. 'In 1845, following the death of Jangir Khan, the position of khan was abolished and the area gradually came under Russian civil administration'; the infobox says 1849.

certainty.note: A nomad pasture grant with no surveyed border; the page gives an area but no frontier.

sources.title: Bukey Horde
sources.note: Founded 1801, khans Bukey, Shygai and Jangir, lands of about 71,000 km2, capital Khan Ordasy, khan abolished 1845 (infobox 1849).

notes: Written for batch ia-03-x from one page (BH). Type colony: a Kazakh khanate under Russian protection, drawn as a vassal tint of the Russian Empire. BH gives the area (71,000 km2), the founding (1801) and the end (1845 in the text, 1849 in the infobox; 1845 is followed), but no frontier and no place: the lands lie between the Volga and Ural rivers on other sources not opened, and the Zhanibek radius is a reading. The kazakh-khanate dossier (ia-03-a) names this horde as a needed counterpart; no gain or loss is recorded against the Kazakh states because BH says only that Russia let the Sultan settle.
